items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: The interviewee mentions Eddie Vincent in the context of Joe Oliver's history ('Eddie Vincent come here and got, uh, Joe Oliver') and later discusses Eddie's saxophone playing and interactions with Joe Oliver, but does not describe a direct personal relationship between himself and Eddie.

ctx.x: Uh, Bunk used to talk about a fellow they called Mustache that ran that place. Some Italian.

Yeah, he did. Now, You take, uh, Louis played, Play, There's fifteen. Then, uh, You take Manuel and them had the coppery, Or had the economy hall. Manuel Perez. That's right. Manuel and them left here. Around in eighteen. Manuel and them left here. Then, Ori, Joe, Oliver. Baby, Dot and them. They took the economy hall. Eddie Vincent come here and got, uh, Joe Oliver. 된된된된된된된 Then Louis, you take, Piro had the boat. Piro and Peter and them had the boat. But still yet they had a contract for the halfway house back…
Was that for the boat then?

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: I believe, uh, my Aunt Handley. Handley was playing clarinet.

ctx.x: I don't know Dad. That Vincent, his name is Vincent.

Yeah, Vincent, that's him. He was playing clarinet. I believe, uh, my Aunt Handley. Handley was playing clarinet. I kept him all around, because he was sitting in good clarinet. Yeah, that's what they say. He was a good clarinet. Yes, sir. And I say, you're too good to stay over here. That's why I brought him over here. And he used to play for the, what they say, in the, not the palace, that was broken. Larrick? Larrick.
